description: British jewellery and accessories brand selling personalised necklaces, bracelets, watches and bags, built around creator-led marketing through its tiered Abbott Lyon Collective advocate community.

evidence.summary: Abbott Lyon's own Collective terms of service state that advocates who complete the starter challenges receive a $150 product voucher and 15% commission on sales, with points and tiers unlocking bigger rewards as they level up.

The brand's own Collective programme page invites content creators (18+, UK-based, 1K+ followers) to join, promising up to 25% commission as members level up, product vouchers worth over £1,000 in total, personalised follower discounts and chances to be featured on the Abbott Lyon Instagram page.
Shopper's partnership listing for Abbott Lyon describes an affiliate payout of 5-10% per sale through its platform, a separate lower route than the brand's own Collective terms.

name: Abbott Lyon

reasons.compensation: The brand's own terms publish 15% commission on sales at the entry tier, rising to up to 25% at higher tiers per its programme page, plus product vouchers — strong published cash terms.
reasons.contact_access: A public programme page with a join route into the brand's own community platform; no public email was found, so it sits below the top band.
reasons.credibility: Established UK jewellery brand with a large social following and a long-running, publicly documented creator programme.
reasons.niche_fit: Personalised jewellery and accessories made for gifting and outfit content — a core fashion-creator niche with highly visual, demonstrable products.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Applications are publicly open to UK creators aged 18+ with 1,000+ followers per the programme page.
reasons.ugc_evidence: A formal, tiered creator community (the Collective, run on Duel) with content challenges, posting requirements, brand reposting rights and Instagram features built into the programme design.

description: Youth group-travel operator founded in 1962, running guided tours for 18-35 year olds to 350+ destinations across six continents, sold direct through contiki.com.

evidence.summary: Contiki's own US affiliate page states the programme is free to join, pays a 5% minimum commission on each confirmed online booking (higher rates for top publishers), and uses a 90-day referral cookie.
LinkClicky's directory lists Contiki's affiliate programme on the Impact platform at 5% commission per booking, described as the rate officially listed with the programme.

Contiki's own Rep Program page describes a creator-facing sister scheme (run via Commission Factory in AU) with commission tiers of 5%, 7.5% and 10% based on travellers booked, a 90-day cookie, and links/promo codes for social promotion.

name: Contiki

opportunity.title: Contiki Affiliate Program (5% minimum commission, 90-day cookie)

reasons.compensation: Published 5% minimum commission on the brand's own page; on multi-thousand-dollar tour bookings that is a large absolute payout per sale, with higher tiers published for the Rep scheme (to 10%).
reasons.contact_access: A public affiliate page on contiki.com with a sign-up route and a named dedicated affiliate management team.
reasons.credibility: Operating since 1962 as part of The Travel Corporation, one of the world's largest guided-tour groups.
reasons.niche_fit: Group tours built exclusively for 18-35 travellers — the exact demographic travel creators reach, with trips that generate weeks of content per booking.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Free public sign-up for websites and bloggers via the brand's affiliate page; Rep applications accepted from US, UK, AU, NZ and Canada.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Contiki runs both a standard affiliate programme and a creator-specific Rep Program with trackable links and promo codes for Instagram, TikTok and YouTube promotion.

description: Singapore-based online travel platform in the Booking Holdings group, selling hotel and accommodation bookings (plus flights and activities) across 1.8M+ properties worldwide, with an in-house partner programme and a creator Ambassador scheme.

evidence.summary: Agoda runs its affiliate programme in-house through Agoda Partners (partners.agoda.com) with tiered commission on departed bookings: 4% for 1-50 monthly departures, 4.5% for 51-300 and 5% for 301+, paid on completed stays.
A September 2026 check of Agoda's own partner pages confirms the published tiers (4% below 50 completed bookings a month, 4.5% from 50, 5% from 300) on booking value, run in-house.

Agoda's own Ambassador page recruits creators with 3,000+ followers on one platform to earn promo-code commission — but its FAQ caps earnings at a maximum of $10 per booking (4% for the first 99 bookings, 5% after), so that creator route is per-booking capped despite 'no limits' headline language about booking count.

name: Agoda

reasons.compensation: Published tiered rates on the Partners programme start at 4% of booking value and rise to 5% (higher via some partner channels); the separate Ambassador code route is capped per booking, which holds this below the top band.
reasons.contact_access: A public Partner Center sign-up at partners.agoda.com plus a public Ambassador application form on agoda.com.
reasons.credibility: Booking Holdings subsidiary founded in 2005, with roughly 1.8M+ properties and operations in 28 countries.
reasons.niche_fit: One of the largest hotel-booking platforms in Asia-Pacific and a Booking Holdings brand — hotel content is a staple of travel creator output.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Applications are publicly open but approval-based; the Ambassador scheme requires 3,000+ followers on a single platform.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Agoda runs a dedicated creator Ambassador scheme (promo codes, campaign features) alongside its publisher programme, though the Ambassador route caps commission at $10 per booking.

description: Edinburgh-founded travel metasearch engine used by 160M+ people a month to compare flights, hotels and car hire across 180 countries, monetising referrals to airlines and OTAs rather than selling travel itself.

evidence.summary: Skyscanner's affiliate programme runs exclusively through Impact and pays a 20% revenue share of the commission Skyscanner itself earns per referred booking (top performers up to 50%), on a 30-day cookie with a $10 minimum payout — the percentage is of Skyscanner's referral income, not of the booking value.

Referly's programme summary, drawn from Skyscanner's own materials, confirms the programme is managed on Impact, pays a flexible performance-based percentage of Skyscanner's partner commission (no fixed headline rate is published by Skyscanner), and requires 5,000+ monthly unique visitors for website applicants, with social creators directed to a separate Creator Programme.

name: Skyscanner

reasons.compensation: A published 20% base share of Skyscanner's own referral commission (up to 50% for top performers) — a high percentage, but of a small per-booking referral fee rather than of booking value, so absolute earnings per booking are modest.
reasons.contact_access: A public programme page at partners.skyscanner.net with application via Impact and manual review.
reasons.credibility: One of the world's largest travel metasearch brands, operating since 2003 and owned by Trip.com Group.
reasons.niche_fit: The default flight-search brand for travel content; fare comparisons and route finds are highly shareable creator material.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Eligibility gates apply: websites need 5,000+ monthly unique visitors and HTTPS; social applicants need 1,000+ travel-focused followers.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Skyscanner steers TikTok/Instagram/YouTube influencers to a separate Creator Programme and runs the affiliate scheme mainly for publishers, so creator-specific evidence is thinner than for product brands.

description: Indigenous-founded Canadian footwear brand (formerly Manitobah Mukluks) selling mukluks, moccasins and modern winter boots made with Indigenous artists, through its own site and retailers.

evidence.summary: Manitobah's own Affiliate and Creator Program page states commission starts at 6%, with a 60-day cookie, monthly payments to the PayPal address on file in AvantLink/Skimlinks, and expectations aimed at reviewers and social creators with first-hand product experience.

The same official page recruits affiliates and creators to tell Manitobah stories with a unique link, offers first looks at new products and artist collaborations, a content asset database on request, and dedicated programme management and PR support.

name: Manitobah

reasons.compensation: Published starting rate of 6% on the brand's own page with a 60-day cookie — a solid, verifiable base rate for footwear.
reasons.contact_access: A public programme page on the brand's own site with a sign-up step and dedicated programme management named as a benefit.
reasons.credibility: Established Canadian brand (founded 1997) with national retail presence and certified Indigenous ownership, smaller than the global fashion groups in this batch.
reasons.niche_fit: Distinctive winter footwear with a strong story (Indigenous artistry, cold-weather function) that fits fashion, outdoor and travel-wardrobe content.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Public application, though the brand states it looks for an established, engaged audience with footwear-review experience.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand's own page is explicitly an 'Affiliate and Creator Program' seeking reviewers and social storytellers, with content assets and PR support offered to partners.

description: Spanish multinational fashion retailer founded in Barcelona in 1984, designing and selling women's, men's and kids' clothing and accessories through 2,700+ stores in 105 countries and mango.com.

evidence.summary: Uppromote's programme directory states Mango's US affiliate programme is managed on CJ Affiliate with a 6% base commission, rising to up to 10% for top performers, on a 30-day cookie with monthly payouts.
Sovrn Commerce's merchant page independently lists Mango.com at 6% commission per sale with a 30-day cookie, corroborating the 6% base rate.

FlexOffers' Mango (US/MX/AU) listing shows a much lower 0.8% payout with a 7-day cookie, which conflicts with the 6% published by CJ-directory and Sovrn sources; the 6% figure is recorded as the programme base and the FlexOffers figure treated as a sub-network payout, but the conflict is documented here.

name: Mango

reasons.compensation: A 6% base rate corroborated by two network sources, rising to up to 10% for top performers; one sub-network listing conflicts at 0.8%, documented in evidence.
reasons.contact_access: Joining is via the CJ Affiliate network; no public creator contact or brand-side application page was found.
reasons.credibility: One of the world's largest fashion groups, founded 1984, with stores in 105 countries.
reasons.niche_fit: Global high-street fashion with trend-led collections that anchor haul, styling and outfit content across TikTok and Instagram.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application through CJ Affiliate, subject to network approval.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Mango works with affiliates across social and fashion sites per its network listings, but publishes no creator community or ambassador structure of its own.

description: Women's fast-fashion retailer founded in San Francisco in 2006 and now owned by Boohoo Group, selling trend-led clothing, shoes and accessories aimed at Gen Z and millennial shoppers.

evidence.summary: Awin's own merchant profile for the NastyGal UK programme publishes its terms: 2% commission on existing-customer sales, 4% on new-customer sales and 1% on app sales, with up to 90-day commission validation.
Lasso's directory lists NastyGal at 5% per sale with a 30-day cookie, which conflicts with the tiered 1-4% in Awin's current programme terms, so no single rate is recorded.

HerPaperRoute's programme guide describes Nasty Gal's Influencer Initiative, a tiered creator scheme on top of the affiliate programme with gifting at lower tiers and possible flat fees for posts at the top tier, joined via Awin or CJ.

name: Nasty Gal

reasons.compensation: Rates conflict across sources (Awin's own terms: 1-4% by customer type; Lasso: 5%; an older guide: 8%), so the rate is recorded as null with the conflict documented; on any reading the base rate is low.
reasons.contact_access: Joining is via Awin (also listed on CJ); no public brand-side creator contact was found.
reasons.credibility: Well-known brand founded in 2006 and owned by Boohoo Group since 2017, though the parent group's finances have been volatile.
reasons.niche_fit: Trend-led women's fast fashion with a strong Gen Z social following — squarely in the fashion-haul creator niche.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application through Awin, subject to approval.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Beyond the network programme, Nasty Gal runs a tiered Influencer Initiative for creators with gifting and potential paid posts at higher tiers.

description: American lifestyle retailer (URBN group) selling alternative fashion, accessories, beauty and apartment goods to Gen Z and young millennial shoppers through stores and urbanoutfitters.com.

evidence.summary: Lasso's directory lists the Urban Outfitters affiliate programme at 5% per sale with a 24-hour cookie and $50 payout threshold.

ReferralRocket's programme page states the Urban Outfitters programme is run by Rakuten Advertising with a base commission of 2% per sale, conflicting with Lasso's 5% and with creator-focused reviews citing up to 15% via Rakuten/Klarna Creator routes, so no single rate could be verified.

Creator Hero's review describes Urban Outfitters' own creator page (urbanoutfitters.com/en-gb/creator) and registration through Rakuten or the Klarna Creator Platform, evidencing a deliberate creator route alongside the publisher programme.

name: Urban Outfitters

reasons.compensation: Published figures conflict widely (2% Rakuten base per one directory, 5% per Lasso, up to 15% in creator reviews), so the rate is null with the conflict documented.
reasons.contact_access: Joining is via Rakuten Advertising or Klarna Creator; no public brand-side creator email was found.
reasons.credibility: Flagship brand of URBN, a NASDAQ-listed retailer with $5B+ annual revenue.
reasons.niche_fit: Alternative fashion, beauty and apartment goods aimed at Gen Z — one of the most content-friendly assortments in US retail.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application through the networks, subject to approval.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Urban Outfitters maintains a creator page and routes creators through Rakuten and the Klarna Creator Platform, but publishes no programme terms of its own.

description: American footwear company headquartered in Manhattan Beach, California — the world's third-largest footwear brand — selling comfort and performance shoes, apparel and accessories for adults and children.

evidence.summary: LinkClicky's directory lists Skechers' affiliate programme on CJ Affiliate at 8.5% per sale for all regions, described as the rate officially listed with the programme (page updated March 2024).
Creator Hero's US shoe-programme roundup lists Skechers at 5% per sale with a 30-day cookie, conflicting with LinkClicky's 8.5% CJ figure, so no single rate is recorded.

Commission Factory's own advertiser page for Skechers (AU) publishes different regional terms — 2% on full-priced items and 1% on sale items with a 7-day cookie — confirming rates vary sharply by market.

name: Skechers

reasons.compensation: Published US figures conflict (8.5% via CJ per LinkClicky vs 5% in creator roundups, and 1-2% in the AU programme), so the rate is null with conflicts documented.
reasons.contact_access: Joining is via CJ Affiliate; no public brand-side creator contact was found.
reasons.credibility: The world's third-largest footwear brand with $8B+ annual sales.
reasons.niche_fit: Mass-market comfort footwear with huge retail reach; strong for comfort, work-shoe and family content, less fashion-forward than pure style brands.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application through CJ Affiliate, subject to approval.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Skechers recruits influencer affiliates through CJ and creator roundups, but runs no public ambassador community of its own.

description: British bags and luggage brand based in Hampshire, England, selling hand-painted, personalised totes, clutch bags, straw baskets and luggage that can be monogrammed with a name or initials.

evidence.summary: Awin's own merchant profile for Lily and Bean states affiliates can earn up to 15% commission on every sale with a 60-day cookie, and publishes the programme contact email affiliate.lilyandbean.co.uk@gmail.com.

Lasso's directory lists Lily and Bean at 15% per sale with a 90-day cookie; because Awin's own profile phrases the rate as 'up to 15%' (a ceiling, with a shorter 60-day cookie), no base rate is recorded.
The Awin profile describes the brand as hand-painted in its Hampshire, England studio, selling totes, luggage, clutch bags and straw baskets, all personalised with a name or initials.

name: Lily and Bean

reasons.compensation: Awin's own profile advertises up to 15% commission, but as a ceiling with no published base rate, so the rate is null and compensation scored on the strength of the ceiling alone.
reasons.contact_access: A programme contact email is published directly on the Awin merchant profile, plus joining via Awin — above the network-only band.
reasons.credibility: Small independent UK studio brand; established niche following for personalised luggage but limited public company information.
reasons.niche_fit: Personalised bags and luggage sit at the fashion/travel crossover — giftable, monogrammed products that photograph well for creator content.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application through Awin, subject to approval.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The programme is a standard network affiliate offer; no creator community, ambassador scheme or UGC programme was found on the brand's own channels.
